cands.name: Terry Brown
cands.bio: Democrat and litigation attorney in Charlotte. He has represented North Carolina House District 92 (southwest Mecklenburg County) since January 2021 and became House Democratic Whip in 2023. He earned a bachelor's degree at UNC Charlotte and a law degree at Campbell University. He has also worked as a political director and campaign manager.

endorsements.text: For the 2026 race, Ballotpedia lists voter-guide recommendations from Beyond The Ballot (Niayai Lavien) and NC Public School Champions (Taylor, PublicEdTay).
In his 2019 Charlotte City Council run, which he lost in the primary, he was endorsed by the Southern Piedmont Central Labor Council.

cands.gaps: We found no documented statements or actions by Brown on data centers, homestead property taxes, limits on investor or foreign land buying, growth and land protection, immigration or H-1B, gun laws, abortion, or school choice and teacher pay. His campaign site names mental health, small business, education, infrastructure and economic growth as priorities, but gives no specific positions on these topics. The only issue statements found are from his 2019 Charlotte City Council campaign, which covered affordable housing, community policing and transit, so we did not treat them as positions on state-level issues. The state budget items his campaign site credits him with securing are not backed here by an official record. We found no date of birth, and no controversies or foreign ties in the pages reviewed.

local.label: Roots 100: His campaign biography says he was born and raised in Fayetteville, worked as a field organizer in Halifax County and in Raleigh, then settled in Charlotte, where he lives in Steele Creek.

score.why: Raised $0, under $5,000 for this office: too little money to score fairly.

qual.background: He has served in the NC House since 2021 and was elected House Democratic Whip for 2023-24, a caucus leadership post. He is a litigation attorney, a former campaign manager and political director, and a former vice chair of the Charlotte Zoning Board of Adjustment.
qual.why: He has several terms of legislative service and a leadership post, plus a law career. Committee seats and board service were not counted.
